subsystems.name: Stimulating lead
subsystems.role: delivers current to the vagus nerve in the neck.

subsystems.name: Pulse generator
subsystems.role: implanted unit that stores energy and outputs controlled pulses.

subsystems.name: Sensing front end
subsystems.role: watches the body for a signal that a seizure or mood shift is starting.
parts: optional neural recording contacts on the lead

subsystems.name: Detection and control loop
subsystems.role: decides when to trigger, and how much to deliver.

subsystems.name: Clinician programmer
subsystems.role: lets a neurologist read stored events and tune the algorithm.

buildSteps.title: Design the cuff
buildSteps.detail: The helical electrode is dimensioned so it wraps the nerve securely without strangling it, since the device must survive years of neck movement.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the lead
buildSteps.detail: Platinum-iridium contacts are welded to conductors, moulded into silicone and cured, then the lead is coiled and strain-tested.

buildSteps.title: Build the generator
buildSteps.detail: A titanium case is laser-welded around the battery and electronics, with a hermetic feedthrough carrying the lead connection.

buildSteps.title: Write the detection firmware
buildSteps.detail: The algorithm is trained on recordings so that it fires on the target biomarker and stays quiet otherwise; thresholds are set conservatively.

buildSteps.title: Test and sterilise
buildSteps.detail: Units undergo accelerated ageing, electrical safety and biocompatibility testing, then are sterilised and sealed.

buildSteps.title: Implant
buildSteps.detail: The cuff is placed around the left cervical vagus nerve, the lead tunneled under the skin to the chest, and the generator pocketed under the collarbone.

buildSteps.title: Program and titrate
buildSteps.detail: Output current is increased over weeks to a tolerated dose, and detection sensitivity is adjusted using the event log.

buildSteps.title: Monitor and refine
buildSteps.detail: Stored heart-rate and stimulation data are reviewed at clinic visits, and parameters are retuned as seizure patterns change.

prerequisites.why: decades of cardiac pacemaker engineering supply the battery, hermetic packaging and telemetry.
the lead must stimulate the same nerve for years without damaging it.
heart-rate rises precede some but not all seizures, so detection is sensitive to a subset of events; direct brain biomarkers need separate intracranial electrodes.
continuous sensing drains a battery that must last years, and a replacement means another operation.
we can stimulate the nerve but cannot yet predict precisely which brain circuits a given pulse pattern engages.

pathway.milestone: generators that automatically stimulate when they detect a heart-rate rise (commercial since the mid-2010s)
pathway.unlocks: some patients get stimulation at seizure onset rather than on a fixed schedule.

pathway.milestone: closed loops driven by neural rather than cardiac signals, using recording contacts on the nerve or a separate brain electrode
pathway.unlocks: faster, more specific triggering, including for seizures with no heart-rate change.

pathway.milestone: multimodal loops that also track sleep, activity and mood
pathway.unlocks: closed-loop use in treatment-resistant depression and possibly other conditions.

pathway.milestone: adaptive dosing that learns each patient's response over months, plus rechargeable or non-invasive closed-loop variants
pathway.unlocks: fewer replacement surgeries and wider access beyond specialist centres.
